judgment.explanation: 茂弘 is the courtesy name of 王導 (Wang Dao). The candidate evidence from aliases.json confirms 王導字茂弘. In the main text, 茂弘 is mentioned in the context where 周侯 says '我常自言勝茂弘今始知不如也', referring to 丞相 (Wang Dao) who is the Chancellor in this story. The candidate is the historical Wang Dao.
阿春 is identified in annotation 001 as the courtesy name (字) of the Empress Dowager (太后), i.e., 鄭后. The annotation explicitly states '(太后字阿春)'. The candidate 阿春 is the correct historical referent.
裒 is the personal name of 司馬裒 (Sima Pou), the younger son of Emperor Yuan. Annotation 007 says '封裒爲琅邪王' and annotation 005 mentions '琅邪王裒'. The candidate 裒 is the correct historical referent.

協 is the personal name of 刁協 (Diao Xie). Annotation 004 pairs 協 with 刁, identifying this as the full name 刁協. In the main text, 刁玄亮 (Diao Xie's courtesy name) is the one who '獨欲奉少主'. The candidate 協 is the correct historical referent.

The courtesy name match is explicit and the contextual role (the person Zhou Hou compares himself to, who is the Chancellor) confirms identity.

The surface form 王導 is the canonical name of the person. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-023-liu-annotation-006) explicitly quotes 王導 speaking about the succession question ('王導曰立子以德不以年'), which matches the role of 丞相 in the main text who argues before the emperor. The canonical name match is direct and unambiguous.

The surface form 周侯 refers to Zhou Yi (周顗), who held the title of Marquis (侯). The alias registry evidence shows 周侯 used in context. In the main text, 周侯 and 丞相 are explicitly distinguished as two separate people entering together ('先喚周侯丞相入'), and 周侯 is the one who laments '我常自言勝茂弘', confirming he is distinct from Wang Dao. The reference semantics also explicitly state distinctness from 丞相 (sfh1-mention-fe0500aaca15da642026ebcb). The alias registry match for 周侯 → 周顗 is supported by the historical context of the story.

The surface form 丞相 refers to Wang Dao (王導), who held the office of Chancellor. The alias registry evidence explicitly connects 丞相 to 王導. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-023-liu-annotation-006) shows 王導 giving advice on the succession, matching the role of 丞相 in the main text who confronts the emperor ('不審陛下何以見臣'). The reference semantics explicitly state coreference with 王導 (sfh1-mention-d046a27061fefeb68ac108a5) and distinctness from 周侯. The office title match combined with the historical role in the narrative confirms identity.

琅邪王裒 refers to Prince of Langya, named Pou (Sima Pou).
敬后 refers to Empress Jing.
王導 is Wang Dao, the Chancellor.
世子 refers to the heir apparent (Emperor Ming).
宣 is the personal name of the heir (Sima Shao, Emperor Ming).
裒 is the personal name of Sima Pou.
琅邪王 refers to the Prince of Langya (Sima Pou).
法盛 is the personal name of the compiler/author (He Fasheng).
元皇帝 refers to Emperor Yuan (Sima Rui), the founding emperor of Eastern Jin.
帝 refers to Emperor Yuan.
鄭后 refers to Empress Zheng, the consort of Emperor Yuan.
明帝 refers to Emperor Ming (Sima Shao), the crown prince/heir.
簡文 refers to Emperor Jianwen (Sima Yu), whom Emperor Yuan wanted to make heir.
議者 refers collectively to the court officials who discussed the succession.
周王 refers collectively to Zhou (Zhou Yi) and Wang (Wang Dao), the two officials.
諸公 refers collectively to the various high officials.
刁玄亮 is Diao Xuanliang (Diao Xie), a court official who supported the younger son.
少主 refers to the younger prince (Jianwen/Sima Yu), the younger son.
周侯 refers to Zhou Yi, titled as a marquis.
丞相 refers to Wang Dao, the Chancellor.
陛下 is the honorific address to the emperor (Emperor Yuan).
茂弘 is the courtesy name of Wang Dao.
